This combination of high luminosity, multi-month duration, and characteristic bluer-to-redder spectral evolution is highly indicative of a superluminous supernova.

Crucially, the peak of the outburst (around time 59850) is dominated by flux in the reddest available bands (9710 nm and 8590 nm), while the bluer bands (e.g., 3670 nm) show very low or negligible flux even at the event's peak.
